lens.message:
Here's the shift: a rollback we have not rehearsed no longer counts as a rollback we have — recovery capability is defined by rehearsal, not by the mechanism existing. It changes how we approach Atlas rollback and recovery procedures (exercised monthly, not just documented), what our runbooks and recovery docs can claim (a written procedure alone is no longer capability), and who owns recovery readiness (Quinton Fairweather, personally, on a monthly clock).

Check it in one spot, the decision as written:

"Atlas rollback rehearsals run monthly from now on. A rollback we have not rehearsed is a rollback we do not actually have." Key decisions: Cadence — monthly Atlas rollback rehearsals. Owner — Quinton Fairweather. As written, it reads as a scheduling call: a recurring drill goes on the calendar and a name goes next to it.

Through the shift, it reads as a redefinition. Any Atlas recovery path we haven't recently rehearsed is now one we plan around as if it doesn't exist — 'monthly' is the expiry date on recovery capability, and Quinton owns demonstrating it, not just booking it. A rollback that exists in code and docs but has no rehearsal behind it no longer counts as one we have.
